july-2026.title: Grace
july-2026.author: A.M. Shine
july-2026.note: Shine gives the Gothic its old weather back: salt air, isolation, inheritance and the sense that the land has been waiting longer than any person can bear. Grace moves with a slow, tightening dread, drawing its horror from return, memory and the things a place refuses to let go.

july-2026.title: Behind a Mask
july-2026.author: Louisa May Alcott
july-2026.note: Small, sharp and quietly venomous, this is Alcott working with a colder hand. Beneath the manners and drawing-room restraint, Behind a Mask becomes a study of performance, power and the danger of underestimating someone who has learned exactly how to be seen.

july-2026.title: Dead but Dreaming of Electric Sheep
july-2026.author: Paul Tremblay
july-2026.note: Tremblay brings horror into the near future without losing the human unease at its centre. The result is unsettling not because the technology feels distant, but because it feels close enough to touch, with identity, body and consciousness beginning to slip out of shape.

june-2026.title: Land
june-2026.author: Maggie O’Farrell
june-2026.note: A novel of maps, loss and survival, set in post-famine Ireland, where the work of recording a landscape becomes tangled with everything the land has already endured.

june-2026.title: The Correspondent
june-2026.author: Virginia Evans
june-2026.note: A warm, sharp and quietly moving novel told through letters, following Sybil Van Antwerp as she writes her way through family, friendship, regret and the one truth she has never quite managed to send.

june-2026.title: John of John
june-2026.author: Douglas Stuart
june-2026.note: A return to the Hebrides, to family pressure, faith, desire and the difficult pull of home. A tender, heavy novel about fathers, sons and the cost of being known.

may-2026.title: The Lamb
may-2026.author: Lucy Rose
may-2026.note: A girl is raised at the edge of a forest, within a life shaped by ritual, hunger, and a mother’s careful, enclosing love. Strangers are taken in from the cold, fed, and quietly consumed. It is the only world she knows. When that pattern begins to shift, so too does her understanding of what binds her there. Desire, control, and inheritance begin to blur, and the possibility of leaving comes into view. It moves with restraint, allowing the unease to gather slowly. What lingers is not shock, but recognition, and the cost of stepping beyond what has always been.

april-2026.title: Starve Acre
april-2026.author: Andrew Michael Hurley
april-2026.note: A child dies, and something in the landscape begins to shift. What follows is less a haunting than a slow unearthing, grief turning outward, into soil, memory, and something older than both. It moves quietly, almost too quietly at first, but the unease builds in a way that lingers long after stepping away from it.
